stories.title: XRP's 13-week ETF inflow streak ends as Bitcoin and Ethereum outflows continue
stories.summary: XRP exchange-traded funds posted an outflow, ending a run of 13 straight weekly inflows. Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs kept losing assets over the same period. The pullback spans all three major crypto ETF categories.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows are a direct gauge of institutional demand. A simultaneous reversal across XRP, Bitcoin, and Ethereum funds points to broader cooling, not a single-asset story.
whatToWatch: Next week's ETF flow reports for XRP, Bitcoin, and Ethereum
Whether XRP inflows resume or the outflow persists
questions: What caused the broad pullback across all three funds?
Is this a short-term rebalancing or the start of a longer trend?

stories.title: Tether loses nearly $5 billion in exchange liquidity to USDC and RLUSD
stories.summary: Tether's USDT lost close to $5 billion in liquidity across crypto exchanges. Rival stablecoins USDC and RLUSD gained ground, reportedly by paying to attract that liquidity. The shift signals rising competition in the stablecoin market.
stories.whyItMatters: Stablecoin liquidity shapes trading costs and depth across exchanges, and a shift away from Tether could reshape which stablecoins dominate crypto trading.
whatToWatch: Whether USDC and RLUSD keep gaining exchange liquidity
Any response from Tether to defend its market position
questions: Why are rivals paying for liquidity now?
How much of this liquidity shift is temporary versus structural?

sources.title: Tether loses nearly $5 billion across crypto exchanges as USDC and RLUSD rivals pay to win liquidity

stories.title: Strategy's discretionary cash falls 72% as buyback authorization rises to $3 billion
stories.summary: Strategy, the large corporate holder of bitcoin, reported a 72% drop in discretionary cash. At the same time, the company raised its share buyback authorization to $3 billion. The two moves together raise questions about how the buyback will be funded.
stories.whyItMatters: Strategy's balance sheet is closely tied to bitcoin's price, so a sharp cash decline alongside a bigger buyback plan affects risk for anyone watching bitcoin-linked equities.
whatToWatch: Whether Strategy executes buybacks under the new $3 billion authorization
Future disclosures on Strategy's cash and debt position
questions: What drove the 72% drop in discretionary cash?
Will the buyback be funded by new debt or equity issuance?

stories.title: Ethereum's faster zk-proofs face Vitalik Buterin's proposed hard cost limit
stories.summary: Ethereum's zero-knowledge proof systems have gotten faster, but Vitalik Buterin is now pushing for a hard limit on proof costs. The proposal would set a firm ceiling rather than let costs float with technical progress. It marks the next stage of debate over how Ethereum scales.
stories.whyItMatters: Proof costs directly affect how cheap and decentralized Ethereum's scaling (layer-2) systems can be, so this debate shapes the network's long-term technical direction.
whatToWatch: How the Ethereum community and researchers respond to the proposed limit
Any formal proposal or timeline for implementation
questions: What specific cost limit is being proposed?
How would the limit affect smaller or independent provers?

sources.title: Ethereum’s faster proofs face Vitalik’s next test: a hard cost limit

stories.title: Wall Street's Bitcoin bears quietly retreat despite recent plunge toward $80,000
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell toward the $80,000 level, a sharp decline from recent highs. Despite that drop, Wall Street short-sellers reportedly pulled back their bearish bets rather than add to them. The quiet retreat contrasts with the price action.
stories.whyItMatters: Institutional positioning often signals how professional investors read a price move, so bears stepping back during a plunge suggests they see the drop as overdone or temporary.
whatToWatch: Further bitcoin price action around the $80,000 level
Updated institutional positioning data
questions: What prompted bears to retreat during a declining market?
Does this shift reflect a change in institutional outlook or just reduced conviction?

sources.title: Wall Street’s Bitcoin bears quietly retreated despite recent plunge toward $80,000

stories.title: XRP holders can now earn fees from Kraken's DeFi customers, with a catch
stories.summary: Kraken has rolled out a feature letting XRP holders earn fees generated by its DeFi customers. The arrangement extends XRP's use beyond simple holding or trading. Kraken's offering reportedly comes with a notable condition for participants.
stories.whyItMatters: The move expands XRP's role in decentralized finance and could influence how holders use the token, though the attached condition may limit its appeal.
whatToWatch: Details on the catch tied to the fee-earning feature
Uptake among XRP holders after launch
questions: What exactly is the catch mentioned for participants?
How competitive are the fees compared to other DeFi options?

stories.title: Cipher's $850 million AI bet draws scrutiny as miner's stock plunges 52%
stories.summary: Bitcoin miner Cipher committed $850 million toward an AI-related investment. Following the announcement, the company's stock fell 52%. Investors are reportedly increasing scrutiny of the move and its risks.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin miners pivoting into AI infrastructure is a broader industry trend, and a steep stock drop raises questions about how markets view that diversification.
whatToWatch: Investor and analyst commentary on Cipher's AI strategy
Cipher's stock performance in coming weeks
questions: Why did the stock fall so sharply on this news?
How will Cipher fund the $850 million commitment?

stories.title: Aave's proposed USAT gateway could block the return swap after a deposit
stories.summary: A new Aave governance proposal would add a gateway for the USAT stablecoin. Under the proposal, users who deposit through this gateway may not be able to swap back out the way they currently can. The change would alter how that deposit path works.
stories.whyItMatters: Changes to deposit and withdrawal paths affect how freely DeFi users can move funds, which matters for anyone relying on Aave's liquidity.
whatToWatch: The outcome of Aave's governance vote on the proposal
Any community pushback over the restricted return swap
questions: Why would the gateway cut off the return swap?
How many users currently rely on that swap path?

stories.title: Binance's SOXL price mark fell 5.9% despite a 3% price band
stories.summary: A tokenized SOXL product on Binance showed a 5.9% drop in its mark price, even though the exchange has a 3% price band meant to limit such moves. The gap suggests the band did not function as expected in this instance.
stories.whyItMatters: Pricing anomalies on tokenized stock products raise questions about the reliability of the mechanisms meant to protect traders from sudden mark-price swings.
whatToWatch: Any explanation or fix from Binance for the pricing gap
Whether similar issues appear on other tokenized products
questions: Why did the 3% band fail to hold the price move?
Were other tokenized assets on Binance affected similarly?

stories.title: Circle drops USDC redemption surcharges while Express keeps its 0.05% fee
stories.summary: Circle has removed surcharges that applied to USDC redemptions. Its Express redemption service, however, keeps a 0.05% fee. The change lowers the cost of converting USDC back to cash through standard channels.
stories.whyItMatters: Redemption costs affect how easily holders can exit USDC, so removing surcharges could make the stablecoin more attractive relative to competitors.
whatToWatch: Any shift in USDC redemption volumes following the change
Whether Circle adjusts the Express fee in the future
questions: Why did Circle remove the surcharges now?
Why does the Express service keep its fee while standard redemption does not?
